correctness.rationale: A direct mathematical proof reconstructs the cyclic one-ascent rigidity, the impossibility of a lone non-unit boundary, the complete three-arc decomposition with two boundary ascents, the gcd-periodic subset lemma, the exact t c/g and t a/g increments, and the forced equality a=c=g, t=1. The reverse classification yields a bijection for all n>=3. Independently run C++ target-exhaustive n=3..6 and Python construction checks n=3..50 match the claimed count, and the known order-six table gives 2160. Infinite correctness relies on the proof, not the finite runs.

originality.rationale: The parent 2026 article only gives the isolated extremal gap and small complete tables; the closest same-author companion article proves the boundary coefficient for the proper cyclic row-permutation subfamily and tabulates all Latin squares only through n=6. The unrestricted all-order divisor-sum formula and unique three-arc classification are not implied by either. Indexed searches were inconclusive as proofs of absolute novelty; unindexed identical work is the residual risk.
residual_risks: Undiscovered or unindexed all-order equivalent classification may exist; database absence alone cannot prove absolute novelty.

value.rationale: The coefficient lies at the first attainable level beyond a sharp published lower-support gap, and computing it for unrestricted Latin squares is mathematically natural but generally difficult. The proof supplies an all-order divisor-sum theorem and a complete unique three-arc/residue-class structural classification, with nontrivial composite-order additional families; it goes materially beyond the previously tabulated n<=6 finite values.
